title: api: standardize rate limit semantics, idempotency, Retry-After and error codes (openai-compat)
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: customer-facing inconsistency in rate limit behavior and error payloads caused confusion for consumers (notably OpenAI-compat clients). This PR unifies rate limit semantics across the Redwood API surface and the OpenAI compatibility layer: 1) canonicalize 429 responses to include a standardized error.code, error.type, and a top-level Retry-After header in seconds when throttled; 2) formalize idempotency key handling for create/generate endpoints (idempotency-key header + deterministic 409/202 behavior); 3) normalize transient server errors with consistent retryable error codes and documentation; 4) improve streaming stability by making Retry-After and retry signals available early in the stream open event and adding recoverable chunk markers for resumable streams; 5) align function/tool-calling errors and structured output validation errors to an OpenAI-compatible schema so SDKs can rely on consistent shapes. Changes include server-side middleware, updated OpenAPI schema, updated openai-compat layer translation, integration + unit tests, and docs/migration notes. Checklist: [x] middleware and rate limiter tests, [x] idempotency integration tests, [x] streaming e2e tests, [x] OpenAPI schema updated, [x] migration doc and changelog entry, [x] perf canary green. Backwards compatibility: default behaviors preserved but clients relying on legacy error strings should follow the migration guide. See linked Linear tasks for rollout plan and telemetry additions.

release_notes: Unified 429 responses now include a structured error object with 'code' and 'type' and a Retry-After header (seconds).
Standardized idempotency-key handling for generate/chat endpoints: store deterministic result and return 409 when conflict is detected, with guidance for clients to retry safely.
Streaming: Retry-After is surfaced as an initial metadata event to enable resumable streams; streaming clients should handle metadata frames before token frames.
OpenAI-compat layer: error shapes normalized to OpenAI-compatible schema; SDKs may need minor updates (see migration docs).
No breaking changes by default, but clients relying on legacy error strings should follow the migration guide.
